name: R. C. Sproul
role: Presbyterian theologian, teacher, and founder of Ligonier Ministries
summary: American Reformed theologian who made classic Calvinist theology accessible to lay audiences through teaching, books, radio, and Ligonier Ministries, and who became a leading defender of biblical inerrancy and justification by faith alone.

key_dates.label: Graduates from Pittsburgh Theological Seminary; goes on to study at the Free University of Amsterdam
Founds the Ligonier Valley Study Center in western Pennsylvania
Helps produce the Chicago Statement on Biblical Inerrancy
Moves Ligonier Ministries to the Orlando, Florida, area
Founds Saint Andrew's Chapel in Sanford, Florida

accomplishments.text: Founded Ligonier Ministries (1971), which spread Reformed theology to a wide lay audience through teaching series, conferences, Tabletalk magazine, and the radio program Renewing Your Mind.
Wrote more than 100 books, including The Holiness of God (1985), his best-known work, and Chosen by God (1986), a defense of the Reformed doctrine of predestination.
Was a leader of the International Council on Biblical Inerrancy and helped produce the Chicago Statement on Biblical Inerrancy (1978).
Defended justification by faith alone against the 1994 Evangelicals and Catholics Together statement, in books such as Faith Alone (1995).
Served as general editor of the New Geneva Study Bible (1995), later the Reformation Study Bible.
Taught philosophy and theology at colleges and seminaries, and later founded Saint Andrew's Chapel (1997) and Reformation Bible College (2011) in Florida.

original.reference: His long-running motto, used as the title of his Tabletalk column

persecution_note: R. C. Sproul was never arrested, imprisoned, or persecuted.
excommunication_note: R. C. Sproul was never excommunicated or disciplined by any church. He was ordained in the mainline United Presbyterian Church and later served as a teaching elder in the Presbyterian Church in America.

sources.citation: R. C. Sproul, The Holiness of God (Wheaton, IL: Tyndale House, 1985).
